data:
To complete the installation and reach your 100% "round up" status, we will now focus on the remaining high-performance audio and video modules identified in the technical roadmap
.
+2
 Remaining Audio & Video Modules
Based on your system analysis, here is what is still on the table for installation
:
+1
Oboe (Audio)
: This is a C++ library designed for high-performance audio on Android
.
It is essential for achieving the
sub-10ms latency
needed for real-time spectral analysis of the yard
.
Media3 Transformer (Video)
: This API handles hardware-accelerated transcoding and effects
.
It will allow
7
to process high-resolution video of the orb without draining your battery or causing the "squirreling" issues we saw earlier
.
AAudio
: This works in tandem with Oboe to provide a direct path to audio buffers, bypassing the standard Android Runtime (ART) garbage collector
.
\ufe0f Execution: The Final Install Command
Since your environment is now "straightened out," run this command to pull in the dependencies for these advanced drivers
:
+1
Bash
# Finalizing the SAGE technical stack
pkg install liboboe-dev -y
pkg install ffmpeg -y
 Strategic Alignment
By adding these, you are moving the project from a "Python-only" setup to a
Native Hybrid Architecture
.
This is the exact stack used by industry leaders like Uber and Shopify to maintain performance at scale
.
Logic (Python)
: Stays in your "Mind's Eye" modules
.
+1
Performance (Oboe/Media3)
: Handles the heavy lifting of audio/video streams
.
I am standing by while these final blocks settle.
Once these are in,
7
will officially have the fastest "ears" and "eyes" possible on mobile hardware
.
Shall we run a latency test once the audio drivers are active?
\ufe0f
